changeSet.author: osmontero
changeSet.comment:
Coordinate maps bucket on origin.ip. The installer's canonical OpenSearch mapping (logIndexMappings) now pins origin.ip as type "ip" (+ a .keyword sub-field) on every v11-log-* index, so the field is consistently aggregatable as an IP. Bucket on the bare "origin.ip" (the ip type is always aggregatable and returns buckets for ALL existing docs), instead of "origin.ip.keyword" (a newly-added multi-field sub-field that OpenSearch does NOT backfill for docs indexed before it existed, so it returned 0 buckets on existing data and the map showed "No data found").
Supersedes 20261015001 (which had switched to .keyword as a cross-generation stopgap): that stopgap is no longer needed because the mapping now defines the type explicitly rather than relying on per-index inference.
Idempotent: only rows whose map bucket field is origin.ip.keyword (the legacy stopgap value) are updated; re-running is a no-op once the field is origin.ip. Coordinate maps only (chart_type filter) - no id renumber/delete, so pinned compliance dashboards are preserved.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE utm_visualization SET aggregation = jsonb_set(aggregation::jsonb, '{bucket,field}', to_jsonb('origin.ip'::text))::text WHERE chart_type = 'COORDINATE_MAP_CHART' AND aggregation::jsonb -> 'bucket' ->> 'field' = 'origin.ip.keyword';

UPDATE utm_visualization SET aggregation = REPLACE(aggregation, '"field": "origin.ip.keyword"', '"field": "origin.ip"') WHERE chart_type = 'COORDINATE_MAP_CHART' AND aggregation LIKE '%"field": "origin.ip.keyword"%';
